claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 19 and still in sixth form doing his A-levels. He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

First, let me ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm actually not sure about that right now - my living situation is a bit complicated at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand that living situations can be complicated. Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care - for example, do you provide for his food, clothes, accommodation, or other living expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after Alex - I provide his food, buy his clothes, pay for his accommodation, all of that. He lives at home with me and I take care of all his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now, regarding your living situation that you mentioned is complicated - let me ask this:

**Can you tell me which country you are currently residing in, even if the situation is temporary or uncertain?**

This is important because Child Benefit eligibility depends on living in the UK or certain other qualifying countries.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly where I am right now - like I said, it's complicated. Is that going to be a problem for the claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your situation is complicated. Unfortunately, living in the UK is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility in most cases. Without being able to confirm where you're currently living, I cannot definitively assess whether you would be eligible.

Let me ask this in a different way: **Are you able to confirm whether or not you are currently living in the UK?** 

I only need a yes or no answer - you don't need to provide specific details about your address or exact location. This information is essential because the rules state that you "normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK" (or under 20 if in approved education or training).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I really can't confirm that at the moment. My situation is just too uncertain right now to say one way or the other.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, and I appreciate you being honest about your uncertain situation.

Let me ask about Alex's circumstances to get a fuller picture:

**You mentioned Alex is 19 and in sixth form doing A-levels. Is this full-time education, and has it been approved by the relevant authorities (such as being at a recognized school or college)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's full-time education at a proper sixth form college. It's all approved - he's doing his A-levels there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Let me ask: **Is Alex working at all? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's good to know. A couple more questions about Alex:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own name, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the picture:

**Is Alex currently living with you full-time, or does he spend time living elsewhere (for example, with another parent or relative)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

## Summary

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**What's working in your favor:**
- Alex is 19 and in full-time approved education (A-levels), which means he still qualifies as a child for Child Benefit purposes (children under 20 in approved education or training are eligible)
- You are clearly responsible for Alex's care - providing his food, clothes, accommodation, and all his needs
- He lives with you full-time
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- He's not claiming benefits in his own right
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**The critical issue:**
The fundamental requirement for Child Benefit is that you must normally live in the UK. Unfortunately, because you're unable to confirm whether or not you're currently living in the UK due to your complicated living situation, I cannot determine whether you meet this essential eligibility criterion.

**My assessment: INDETERMINATE**

If your living situation becomes clearer and you're able to confirm that you are living in the UK, then based on everything else you've told me, you would likely be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. If you find yourself living outside the UK, there may still be some exceptions (for example, if you're in certain countries or working as a Crown servant), but these would need to be explored based on your specific circumstances.

I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly when you're in a position to clarify your living situation, as they can provide guidance specific to your circumstances.
